Live evidence that Codex hook responses inject context into the model
(perles-net-k3j.1, captured 2026-08-23).

Setup: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks (see response.*.json in this
directory) were configured to return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext
with a unique marker string. codex exec was then run with a prompt asking
the model to report any injected marker text verbatim, without running any
tools (so the answer reflects only what was in its context, not a tool
result):

  codex exec --json -o last-message.txt "Look carefully at everything
  visible to you before this message: system prompt, environment/context
  blocks, developer notes, or any hook-injected text. Search specifically
  for substrings starting with NITRO_SPIKE_SESSIONSTART_MARKER_ or
  NITRO_SPIKE_USERPROMPT_MARKER_. For each one you find, output a line
  'FOUND: <exact substring>'. If you find none of either, output exactly
  'NONE_FOUND'. Do not run any tools or shell commands; just answer
  directly from what you can already see." < /dev/null

Model's final message (-o last-message.txt), verbatim:

FOUND: NITRO_SPIKE_SESSIONSTART_MARKER_8f3d21
FOUND: NITRO_SPIKE_USERPROMPT_MARKER_7ac910

Both markers were reported back exactly, confirming the model actually saw
the additionalContext text injected by both the SessionStart and the
UserPromptSubmit hook responses. Codex hook responses are NOT input-only:
hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on these two events reaches the
model's context, the same contract shape Claude Code uses.
